In version control, a branch is an isolated, private area to keep your code changes separate from the main-line code (repository). Multiple developers who work on a particular feature share code in the branch:
They push (commit) those components that are needed for the feature from the snapshot into the branch.

Each time a component is committed into the branch, a new version of it is created in the branch. The branch preserves the older versions of a component if a new version replaces it; thus, accidental overwrite of code becomes a non-issue.
